full.description: This image is a gross specimen photograph of a cross-section of a human heart. The organ exhibits marked thickening of the left ventricular myocardium, which significantly reduces the internal chamber cavity size. These findings are characteristic of pronounced left ventricular hypertrophy. The myocardium appears dense and muscular, consistent with chronic pressure overload.

blind.description: This is a gross pathology photograph of a human heart. The specimen demonstrates marked left ventricular hypertrophy and structural alterations. These findings are characteristic of chronic rheumatic heart disease, potentially involving a prosthetic mitral valve. The visual features are consistent with long-standing hemodynamic overload affecting the cardiovascular system.

random.description: This image shows a gross specimen cross-section of the heart. The ventricular walls are markedly thickened, particularly the septum and free wall, showing concentric left ventricular hypertrophy. The chambers appear somewhat compressed due to the severe hypertrophy of the myocardium. This appearance is characteristic of hypertrophic cardiomyopathy.
